The Stinger was introduced in 2479 as the second mass-produced reconnaissance BattleMech, designed by Earthwerks Incorporated to meet the Terran Hegemony's urgent demand for scout 'Mechs. Its creation sparked a twenty-year legal dispute with General Mechanics, who accused Earthwerks of copying their Wasp design, a case ultimately dropped due to mounting legal costs. Production proved extraordinarily prolific, with over 200,000 units manufactured before the fall of the Star League, making it arguably the most-produced BattleMech in history.

The devastating Succession Wars reduced operational numbers to approximately 5,000 by 3025, yet the Stinger's ubiquity ensured its survival where more sophisticated designs perished. Manufactured across dozens of facilities throughout the Inner Sphere and Periphery, the Stinger filled the essential role of scout and trainer for centuries, its simple construction and widespread availability making it an enduring fixture of BattleMech warfare.

The Stinger fulfills its reconnaissance role through exceptional mobility rather than firepower. Its GM 120 fusion engine propels the twenty-ton chassis to speeds exceeding 90 kilometers per hour, while six Chilton 360 jump jets provide 180 meters of jump capability, sufficient to escape most pursuers or traverse difficult terrain. The weapons loadout reflects this philosophy: an Omicron 3000 medium laser serves as the primary armament, supported by twin LFN Linblad machine guns that proved devastating against infantry, earning the Stinger a fearsome reputation among ground troops until the Firestarter's introduction.

Three tons of Riese-100 armor provides only modest protection, typical for light 'Mechs but insufficient against sustained fire. Heat management poses no concern, as the ten single heat sinks easily dissipate the minimal thermal output. The fine-tuned hand actuators proved beneficial for salvage work and objective retrieval during raids.

The Stinger's most notorious weakness is its cramped cockpit, which forces pilots of average build to squeeze into the control seat and often requires technician assistance to exit, the reverse of feudal knights who needed squires to mount their steeds. The Dynatec 990 targeting system remains adequate if unremarkable, retained more for cost efficiency and ease of manufacture than effectiveness.

The Strider was introduced in 3057 as one of the earliest Inner Sphere OmniMechs to reach the battlefield. Developed by Luthien Armor Works, the design was considered by many critics to be something of a disappointment, primarily due to LAW's decision to base the new OmniMech on the chassis of the venerable Cicada. Proponents of the original design noted that while the Strider sacrificed the Cicada's exceptional speed for improved armor and firepower, this loss meant the 'Mech could not escape without serious support if outmatched by heavier opponents.

Despite initial criticism, the Strider proved itself a capable platform for the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery. By the time of the Word of Blake Jihad, the design had become commonplace among elite Kuritan commands, often serving as a light lance command 'Mech or reconnaissance unit for heavier formations. Irian BattleMechs Unlimited secured a production license by 3067, expanding the Strider's availability to Free Worlds League forces as well.

The Strider is built on an Alshain Type KR240 endo-steel chassis powered by a GM 240 fusion engine, reducing maximum speed to 97 kilometers per hour compared to the Cicada's 129. This trade-off provides seven and a half tons of StarSlab/4 armor with CASE protection, making the Strider considerably more durable than its progenitor. Twelve tons of pod space allow for significant weapons and equipment variety across different configurations.

A notable limitation stems from LAW's decision to employ standard heat sinks rather than double-capacity models, restricting the thermal efficiency of most configurations. Consequently, nearly every standardized loadout features arm-mounted missile pods supported by lasers or electronic equipment in the torso bays. The Prime configuration exemplifies this approach with twin Artemis-enhanced SRM-6 launchers, a Beagle active probe for reconnaissance duties, and a small laser for emergency defense. The F configuration, nicknamed the "Grand Jenner" by DCMS pilots for its similarity to that famous light 'Mech, combines Streak SRM-4 launchers with medium lasers and jump jets, and is widely considered the most effective standard configuration.

Luthien Armor Works developed the Strider as part of the Draconis Combine's effort to field domestically-produced OmniMechs following the Clan Invasion. Rather than attempt a clean-sheet design, LAW engineers chose to adapt the proven Cicada chassis, accepting reduced speed in exchange for the flexibility inherent to OmniMech technology. The resulting design entered service in 3057, with the DCMS rushing several production runs to front-line units despite mixed initial reviews.

The Strider's reputation improved steadily as pilots learned to exploit its versatility rather than lamenting its reduced mobility. By the late 3050s, the design had found its niche as a light lance command platform and reconnaissance asset for heavier formations. Several production runs were sold to the Federated Commonwealth during the final months of that nation's existence, with deliveries continuing to both successor states for several years afterward.

Irian BattleMechs Unlimited began licensed production on Shiro III by 3067, expanding the Strider's reach to Free Worlds League commands. The design saw extensive service during the Jihad on multiple fronts, with some configurations adapted to incorporate captured Clan technology during Operation Bulldog. Post-Jihad production has introduced configurations utilizing advanced C3 networks and Clan-specification missile systems, ensuring the Strider remains relevant to modern combined-arms doctrine.

The Sunder is a ninety-ton Inner Sphere OmniMech developed by the Draconis Combine as the assault class component of the DCMS first generation of domestically produced OmniMechs. Introduced in 3056, the design was born from the intensive study of captured Clan Hellbringer and Summoner chassis following the Battle of Luthien in 3052. Draconis Combine engineers at Luthien Armor Works determined the leg assemblies of both progenitor designs could support twenty additional tons of mass, though overcoming catastrophic actuator burnout in prototypes and resolving caustic exhaust fouling from torso-mounted pod bays delayed the Sunder's entry into service, making it among the last of the first-generation DCMS OmniMechs to reach full production.

Though initially a Combine-exclusive design, the Sunder's proven chassis attracted interest from multiple successor states, and licensed production eventually spread the assault OmniMech to militaries across the Inner Sphere. This broad manufacturing base has kept the Sunder in continuous service from the Clan Invasion era through the ilClan period.

The Sunder is built around a Hermes 360 XL engine that propels the ninety-ton chassis to a top speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour. The bulky engine forced designers to relocate the torso OmniPod bays above the cockpit, an arrangement that contributed to early exhaust fouling problems but provides thirty-six tons of available pod space. Sixteen and a half tons of Mitchell Argon armor give the Sunder respectable protection for an assault 'Mech, while fifteen fixed double heat sinks manage the thermal load across most configurations.

In its Prime configuration, the Sunder is built for devastating close-range engagements. An Autocannon/20 forms the core of its firepower, supported by two large lasers for medium-range engagement, a trio of SRM-4 launchers, and two medium lasers. This loadout makes the Prime variant most lethal at short ranges, though the large lasers provide adequate reach to engage enemies closing on its position.

While thirty-six tons of pod space theoretically make the Sunder a powerful combatant, its reduced ground speed and reliance on less efficient Inner Sphere weaponry leave it at a disadvantage compared to many Clan assault OmniMechs. The widespread use of salvaged Clan OmniPods during Operation Bulldog finally allowed the Sunder to compete on more equal footing with designs such as the Warhawk and Executioner.

The Sunder's origins lie in the aftermath of the Battle of Luthien in 3052, when Draconis Combine forces captured examples of the Clan Hellbringer and Summoner OmniMechs. Combine engineers at Luthien Armor Works began an ambitious program to reverse-engineer these designs for domestic manufacture, selecting the assault weight class as one of several parallel development efforts alongside the Avatar and other first-generation OmniMechs. Prototype Sunders suffered from catastrophic actuator failure as the heavier chassis overstressed components designed for lighter Clan machines, and additional problems with caustic exhaust residue from torso-mounted weapons fouling the cockpit canopy and sensor arrays required extensive rework before full production could begin in 3056.

Initial deployment saw Sunders assigned to assault lances stationed along the Clan border, where they played a significant role during Operation Bulldog. The DCMS authorization for widespread use of salvaged Clan weaponry in OmniPods proved transformative, as Sunders equipped with Clan-grade weapons could finally compete favorably against Clan Warhawk and Executioner OmniMechs. Many Sunders also served as the anchor point of DCMS command networks, with dedicated C3 configurations enabling lance and company-level coordination that proved its effectiveness during the conflict.

StarCorps Industries recognized the Sunder's potential and licensed production from Luthien Armor Works in the early 3060s, establishing manufacturing lines at their plants on Crofton, Loburg, Son Hoa, and St. Ives. This licensing arrangement proved fortuitous when the Word of Blake Jihad devastated the DCMS's industrial base. Luthien Armor Works' OmniMech production facility was destroyed during the opening stages of the Jihad, cutting off the Combine's primary source of Sunders. StarCorps continued production for the Federated Suns, Lyran Alliance, and Capellan Confederation, ensuring the design survived even as the DCMS lost access to new production.

The Sunder continued to see combat during the tensions surrounding the Lyons Thumb and throughout the First Combine-Dominion War, where its role as a C3 network anchor proved particularly valuable. In the Dark Age era, new configurations incorporating Clan-spec weaponry and advanced electronics such as C3 boosted slave units and TSEMP cannons demonstrated the chassis's continued relevance. StarCorps facilities on Crofton and Loburg maintained production into the ilClan era, keeping the Sunder in service across multiple successor states long after its original Combine-only production had ended.

The Tempest is a sixty-five-ton heavy BattleMech designed by Irian BattleMechs Unlimited as a replacement for the aging Thunderbolt in Free Worlds League service. Originating in the late 3040s and relying on little advanced technology, the Clan Invasion and resulting research and development effort led to radical modifications, and the production model fielded in 3055 bore little resemblance to the initial concept. Irian BattleMechs Unlimited produces the Tempest at facilities on both Irian and Angell II, and the design has earned a reputation as a versatile and well-balanced heavy combatant that has proven difficult to improve upon. Combat operations have prompted the creation of several variants as both field modifications and factory-built options.

The Tempest's primary armament centers on a Zeus Slingshot Gauss rifle, delivering devastating long-range firepower without generating waste heat. A Sutel Precision Line large pulse laser supplements this at medium to long ranges, while three Diplan M3 medium lasers and an Irian Weapons Works 60mm SRM-6 rack provide punishing close-range firepower. The Gauss rifle carries two tons of ammunition for sixteen rounds of fire, and the SRM-6 has one ton of ammunition providing fifteen salvos.

The original design concept called for twin PPCs, but Irian designers replaced this configuration with the Gauss rifle and large pulse laser combination for the production model. Four Chilton 465 jump jets grant the Tempest a one hundred twenty meter jump capability, allowing it to keep pace with many lighter 'Mechs despite a mediocre cruising speed of forty-three kilometers per hour. Fine-tuning and testing on Irian's varied landscapes led the manufacturer to claim the Tempest operates across any terrain without loss of capability, an assertion the League military has tested on several occasions. Twelve tons of Maximillian 100 armor provide respectable protection for a sixty-five ton chassis, though the lack of CASE leaves the XL engine vulnerable to catastrophic ammunition explosions.

The Tempest's origins trace to the late 3040s, when Irian BattleMechs Unlimited began developing a replacement for the venerable Thunderbolt in Free Worlds League service. The project initially used little advanced technology, but the shock of the Clan Invasion in 3049 prompted massive investment in research and development across the Inner Sphere. The Tempest design was radically overhauled to incorporate newly recovered Star League-era technologies, and the production TMP-3M that rolled off the Irian assembly line in 3055 was fundamentally different from the original prototype.

The Tempest's introduction immediately created friction within the Free Worlds League's defense industry. When Earthwerks attempted to market their updated TDR-9M Thunderbolt variant, Irian BattleMechs Unlimited lobbied the League Central Coordination and Command to halt new Thunderbolt production, arguing the Tempest rendered further Thunderbolt development unnecessary. The resulting corporate dispute was only resolved when the Word of Blake brokered a compromise, pitting the two designs against each other in a combat trial to determine which would supply the Blakist military.

Free Worlds military strategists embraced the Tempest, deploying it throughout the FWLM in formations that deliberately echoed Star League Defense Force doctrine. Lance- and company-sized Tempest units, often paired with the lighter Shadow Hawk, created flexible strike forces capable of rapid offensive and defensive operations. The largest concentrations served in the Marik Militias, Free Worlds Legions, and Fusiliers of Oriente. The design made its greatest impression in the Sirian Lancers, where its balance of firepower and agility proved vital during Operation Guerrero and the subsequent liberation of Sirius and Procyon.

The Jihad devastated the Tempest's production infrastructure. The Irian facility fell under Word of Blake control, and while production continued under Blakist oversight, many Free Worlds League units found themselves cut off from spare parts and replacement chassis. The establishment of the Angell II production line by Irian Technologies helped offset this loss, though the facility did not reach operational capacity until 3077. Following the Jihad, the Republic of the Sphere assumed control of both facilities, allegedly taking the Irian line offline during the 3090s, though production reportedly continued in secret.

The collapse of the Republic and the reformation of the Free Worlds League saw Irian BattleMechs Unlimited regain control of its production lines. Regarded as a difficult design to improve upon, it took until the 3130s for a formal successor variant to debut. New variants including the TMP-4M and the Clan Protectorate-backed Tempest C emerged during the Dark Age, demonstrating the design's continued relevance more than eight decades after its introduction.

The Templar III is a Dark Age era eighty-five ton assault OmniMech produced by General Motors for the Federated Suns. Introduced around 3100, it was designed as a direct replacement for the original Templar after the destruction of Kallon Industries' factory on Talon during the Jihad eliminated production of the first-generation design. General Motors established a new production line on New Valencia to continue the Templar legacy with updated technologies.

Like its predecessor, the Templar III serves primarily as a command 'Mech for AFFS assault formations. The design incorporates advanced equipment across its alternate configurations, giving field commanders significant tactical flexibility while maintaining the assault-weight presence that made the original Templar an effective formation anchor.

The most significant change from the original Templar is the Templar III's adoption of a GM 340 Light engine in place of the KalTek 340 Extralight. This substantially improves survivability by eliminating the vulnerability to side torso destruction that plagued the original design, though it comes at the cost of reduced pod space, dropping from forty tons to twenty-nine. The Kallon Type XX Endo Steel chassis and StarGuard CIV armor maintain the same level of protection as the predecessor, and a Heavy-Duty Gyro improves stability under fire.

The primary configuration draws comparison to the proven WHM-8D Warhammer loadout, mounting twin ER PPCs as its primary armament alongside extended-range medium and small lasers. A four-tube short-range missile launcher provides supplementary close-range firepower, with CASE protecting the ammunition. A targeting computer links all energy weapons for improved accuracy, while four additional double heat sinks manage the considerable thermal output of the energy-heavy weapons suite.

While the reduced pod capacity limits the Templar III's ability to mount the heaviest weapon loadouts, the improved chassis durability ensures it can remain in the fight longer. Several configurations take advantage of advanced and Clan-specification technologies to maximize firepower within the tighter weight budget, making the Templar III a more resilient, if somewhat less versatile, successor to the original.

The Templar III's development grew directly from the ashes of the Jihad. With the Kallon Industries factory on Talon destroyed by the Word of Blake, the Federated Suns lost its only production source for the original Templar. General Motors on New Valencia, already producing the Pendragon, a limited-production design loosely based on the Templar chassis, leveraged their familiarity with the platform to develop a modernized successor. Production of the Templar III began around 3100, establishing New Valencia as the new center of Templar-lineage manufacturing.

The Templar III quickly became a popular command 'Mech for AFFS company and battalion commanders, appearing regularly in assault lances throughout Federated Suns frontline formations. During the Capellan invasion campaigns of the Dark Age, lances of Templar IIIs proved effective in combined arms operations. In one notable engagement on Spica in late 3144, a lance of three Templar IIIs and a Salamander inflicted significant casualties on a Capellan 'Mech company, using ER PPCs and targeting computers to devastating effect while channeling the enemy through minefields and narrow streets.

The Templar III's influence extended beyond the Federated Suns. When General Motors resumed Victor production in the 3080s, they redesigned that venerable assault 'Mech to share many components with the Templar III, creating manufacturing efficiencies on New Valencia. Additionally, the custom configuration piloted by the First Prince demonstrated the platform's ability to accept Clan-specification weaponry, producing a significantly more lethal variant that served through the critical campaigns of the late 3140s and into the ilClan era.

text.overview: Irian’s Stalker II was polarizing. Its extraordinary durability set the new ’Mech up for success, though many potential customers snubbed it on account of the limited flexibility of its weaponry. The new cockpit also made it difficult to pilot. Irian thus developed a new variant of its classic Stalker, keeping the newer ’Mech’s hardened armor. Irian addressed concerns regarding damage output on the modern battlefield by making its primary weapons Clan grade. Irian could supply equivalent large pulse lasers to augment the traditional Magna medium lasers. They negotiated a deal with Skate Khanate’s Beta Aimag for missile launchers and sensors in return for a percentage of the production output. The STK-9F’s combination of durability and destructive potential made it a common sight in this region of the Inner Sphere.
text.notableUnits: Captain Kyree Anansi: Kyree has purposefully obscured her origins. She cropped up several years ago, traveling throughout the Former Free Worlds League in a new Stalker, selling her services while always hiring available mercenaries in short-term contracts to form ad hoc companies. She always had enough of her own cash to keep questions to a minimum. Her name itself is likely a nom de guerre harkening to an ancient Terran “trickster” god. Kyree likely took on the mantle due to a predilection towards feints, ambushes, and other crafty tactics that seem in stark contrast to her lumbering assault ’Mech. Or perhaps she took the name due to her well-documented personal trait—a love of storytelling that further obfuscates any sense of who she really is.

text.notes: Features the following Design Quirks: Ammunition Feed Problems (SRMs).

text.overview: The Starhawk is a 70-ton Clan heavy OmniMech developed by Clan Snow Raven in 2948 during the Golden Century. Born from an ingenious act of engineering improvisation that combined proven components from two existing designs, the Starhawk served as a capable heavy combatant in the Snow Raven touman for several decades before being phased out in favor of newer acquisitions. Though its production run was relatively limited compared to other heavy OmniMechs of its era, the Starhawk remains a notable example of Snow Raven resourcefulness and the modularity inherent in OmniMech technology.
text.capabilities:
Built around a 350-rated XL fusion engine, the Starhawk achieves a top speed of 86 kilometers per hour, placing it among the faster heavy OmniMechs of its era. The chassis mounts 8.5 tons of ferro-fibrous armor, providing reasonable protection for its weight class while freeing tonnage for pod-mounted weaponry. Fourteen fixed double heat sinks manage thermal loads across configurations. The hybrid construction combining Timber Wolf lower-chassis mobility with a Hellbringer-derived torso gives the Starhawk a distinctive combat profile that blends speed with versatile pod capacity.

In its Primary configuration, the Starhawk carries a pair of Ultra Autocannon/10s mounted in each arm, delivering devastating medium-range firepower with the option for increased rate of fire at the risk of jamming. An SRM-6 launcher in the right torso supplements the ballistic payload at close range, while an Active Probe and ECM Suite housed in the left torso provide significant electronic warfare capability. This sensor package allows the Starhawk to detect hidden units while simultaneously disrupting enemy targeting systems, making the Prime configuration well-suited to aggressive reconnaissance-in-force operations.

The Starhawk's armor protection, while reasonable, falls short of heavier OmniMechs in its weight class, and the design's reliance on ammunition-dependent weapons across most configurations leaves it vulnerable in extended engagements where resupply is unavailable. The XL engine, while enabling the design's impressive speed, also increases the risk of a catastrophic kill from torso damage that a standard engine might survive.
text.deployment: The Primary configuration reflects Clan Snow Raven's doctrinal preference for information superiority, typically deploying as a command element in heavy reconnaissance Stars where its integrated sensor suite complements the offensive capability of accompanying OmniMechs. The Active Probe and ECM Suite grant the MechWarrior exceptional situational awareness and the ability to shield nearby Starmates from enemy electronics, while the heavy ballistic armament ensures the Starhawk can hold its own when engagement becomes unavoidable. Snow Raven Star Commanders favored this variant for independent operations where a single heavy 'Mech needed to both gather intelligence and deliver firepower without dedicated support.
text.battleHistory:
The Starhawk's origins lie in Clan Snow Raven's characteristic resourcefulness. In 2948, the Ravens successfully won the Timber Wolf's leg actuator specifications in a Trial against Clan Wolf, one of many such exchanges of technology that characterized the competitive but cooperative nature of the Golden Century. Rather than attempt to replicate the entire Timber Wolf design, Snow Raven engineers recognized that the adaptability of OmniMech gyroscopes would allow them to combine components from different chassis. They paired the Timber Wolf's proven lower assembly with the torso structure of the Hellbringer, producing a new 70-ton OmniMech that entered service as the Starhawk.

Production was established at Industrial Complex Raven Alpha on Lum, one of Clan Snow Raven's primary Homeworld manufacturing centers. The Starhawk served the Raven touman through the latter decades of the Golden Century and into the Political Century that followed, providing a capable heavy OmniMech platform for a Clan that historically invested more heavily in aerospace and naval assets than ground forces. The design saw service during the various inter-Clan conflicts and Trials that marked this period, though the Snow Ravens' preference for avoiding large-scale ground engagements meant the Starhawk saw less sustained combat than contemporary designs fielded by more aggressive Clans.

The Starhawk's production run appears to have been relatively limited in duration. Records indicate the production line was active from approximately the Late Succession Wars era through the second phase of the Clan Invasion, after which production ceased. The most likely explanation is that the Snow Ravens phased out the Starhawk after acquiring the Summoner production line from Clan Ghost Bear, which offered a proven 70-ton OmniMech with a more established combat record and broader logistical support. With the Summoner filling the same weight class niche, maintaining a parallel production line for the Starhawk became unnecessary.

Despite its limited production history, the Starhawk represents an important example of the technological cross-pollination that defined the Golden Century. Its hybrid construction demonstrated the modularity inherent in OmniMech technology, a principle that would be exploited by other Clans in later centuries. Surviving Starhawks likely remained in second-line or solahma units as newer designs replaced them on the front lines, gradually fading from active service as attrition and parts scarcity took their toll.

text.notes: Design Quirks: Bad Reputation, Difficult Ejection, Multi-Trac.

text.deployment: This variant represents an aftermarket modification produced by Mech-it Lube, a mercenary-focused parts supplier that specialized in battlefield refits. This variant trades the twin machine guns for a quartet of small lasers, significantly increasing anti-'Mech capability at close range while maintaining some effectiveness against infantry through concentrated laser fire. The configuration proved popular with mercenary units who valued firepower over the machine guns' ammunition dependency, though the increased heat load requires more careful management from pilots.
text.battleHistory:
The Stinger's journey began in 2479 when Earthwerks Incorporated won the Terran Hegemony's contract to produce a light scout 'Mech. General Mechanics immediately filed suit, claiming the design illegally copied their Wasp, and the resulting legal battle dragged on for twenty years before GM abandoned the effort due to prohibitive costs. Meanwhile, Stinger production continued unabated, eventually outstripping every other BattleMech design, even Earthwerks' own Archer.

During the Star League era, over 200,000 Stingers entered service, spreading to every corner of human-occupied space. The design's simplicity proved advantageous as the Succession Wars devastated technological infrastructure; while complex 'Mechs became irreplaceable, Stingers could still be manufactured and maintained. By 3025, approximately 5,000 remained operational, proof of the era's destructive toll but also to the design's resilience.

Throughout the Succession Wars, the Stinger took on additional duties beyond scouting. Many units pressed them into training roles, replacing the increasingly rare Chameleon training 'Mechs. The iron sights on the machine guns forced cadets to manually aim their weapons, developing motor skills that proved valuable for fine manipulation tasks during objective raids and personnel extractions. Notable actions demonstrated both the limitations and potential of massed light 'Mech tactics, from the disastrous "Charge of the Horde" at Markerson in 3019 to more successful refined approaches that paired Stingers with heavier Jenners for fire support.

Earthwerks remained the largest producer during the Succession Wars era, with facilities on Calloway VI, Keystone, and Grand Base. Coventry Metal Works held the second position until Periphery manufacturers (particularly Vandenberg Mechanized Industries and Pinard Protectorates Limited in the Taurian Concordat) expanded production as CMW shifted focus to the Commando. Other major Periphery producers included Majesty Metals and Manufacturing on Canopus IV and Alliance Defenders Limited on Alpheratz.

The Clan Invasion prompted renewed interest in upgrading the venerable design, with Earthwerks introducing the STG-5M in 3050 using recovered lostech from the Helm Memory Core. Later collaboration between the Taurian Concordat and Word of Blake produced further advanced variants, with the Taurians receiving assistance to kick-start their upgrade program in exchange for large numbers of Stinger and Wasp 'Mechs. These designs were eventually shared with Detroit Consolidated and Hellespont Industrials. By the ilClan era, Clan variants emerged from the Wolf Empire's Keystone factory, continuing the Stinger's tradition of serving every known military force in the Inner Sphere.

text.deployment: This variant takes Mech-it Lube's modifications further, sacrificing the Stinger's signature jump jets entirely in exchange for additional armor protection and two medium lasers. Described by some wags as a miniature version of the "Blazing Inferno" Commando, this variant transforms the nimble scout into a budget fire-support platform. While the loss of jump capability severely limits the 'Mech's reconnaissance effectiveness, mercenary units operating in open terrain appreciated the increased survivability and firepower for frontal engagements.

text.overview:
The Stooping Hawk is a rare anomaly among Clan Blood Spirit designs, a full OmniMech produced by a Clan that traditionally eschewed the technology in favor of cheaper, more rugged BattleMechs. Introduced around 2970, the Stooping Hawk traces its origins to the Ghost Bear OmniMech Prototype A, later known as the Sun Bear, which the Blood Spirits won in a Trial of Possession after the Bears phased the design out in favor of the Mad Dog. Blood Spirit scientists took the captured prototype and developed it to its fullest potential, christening the result the Stooping Hawk.

The design represented a significant philosophical departure for the resource-poor Spirits, whose Khans regularly reviewed the Stooping Hawk's battlefield performance to determine whether its expensive construction justified the ongoing costs. The 'Mech's continued service through the Blood Spirit Annihilation stands as proof of its effectiveness, and Clan Stone Lion subsequently secured the York production facility to continue manufacturing the design.
text.capabilities:
Despite Khan Ceana Boques's demand for a low-cost and rugged design, the Blood Spirit scientist caste built the Stooping Hawk around the more expensive York YT Endo Steel frame and Compound Alpha ferro-fibrous armor to maximize pod space. The scientists recognized, however, that an extralight fusion engine would be a step too far, fitting a standard 275-rated power plant that provides a maximum speed of 86 km/h. This deliberate trade-off sacrifices some pod capacity for battlefield survivability, a critical consideration for a Clan with limited resources to replace losses.

The resulting chassis offers twenty-one and a half tons of pod space, which the Blood Spirits have exploited to field an impressive array of configurations ranging from direct-fire brawlers to missile support platforms. The primary configuration exemplifies this versatility, mounting jump jets for 150-meter leaps alongside an Ultra Autocannon/10 supported by four medium-class lasers. This combination of mobility, firepower, and ammunition endurance makes the Prime particularly well-suited to Trials of Possession, where the Stooping Hawk can exploit terrain and cover to offset its medium weight class.

The design's durability-focused engineering has kept it operational across decades of hard service in the Homeworld Clans, and technicians consistently report that the Stooping Hawk tolerates field damage and rough maintenance conditions better than most OmniMechs of its generation.
text.deployment: Introduced during the Jihad era, the F configuration is optimized for close-quarters combat. The loadout centers on paired Heavy Medium and Medium Pulse Lasers supplemented by Heavy Small Lasers and a Streak SRM-4 launcher. Eight Improved Jump Jets provide exceptional close-range maneuverability, allowing the pilot to close rapidly and maintain optimal engagement distance. Two additional double heat sinks help manage the thermal load of the energy-heavy weapons suite during sustained infighting.
text.battleHistory:
The Stooping Hawk's origins lie in the political maneuvering of the Homeworld Clans during the late Golden Century. When OmniMech technology emerged in 2854, Clan Blood Spirit assumed their chronic resource shortages would prevent them from ever acquiring it. This assessment proved incorrect when Clan Fire Mandrill's Kindraa Smythe-Jewel unexpectedly offered OmniMech technology in exchange for Blood Spirit territory on Foster, giving the Spirits the foundation they needed to begin their own OmniMech development program.

The opportunity to build upon existing OmniMech work came when Clan Ghost Bear phased out its Prototype A (the Sun Bear) in favor of the Mad Dog. The Blood Spirits challenged for and won the Bear prototype in a Trial of Possession, providing their scientists with a proven chassis to refine rather than starting from scratch. The resulting Stooping Hawk was more expensive than the Spirit Khans preferred, but its battlefield performance consistently justified the investment.

The Stooping Hawk served as one of the few OmniMechs in the Blood Spirit touman for over a century, seeing action in the numerous inter-Clan conflicts that characterized Homeworld politics. The design proved its worth repeatedly in Trials and raids, its combination of durability and reconfigurability providing the resource-strapped Spirits with tactical flexibility they could not otherwise afford. Blood Spirit Khans continued to scrutinize the design's cost-effectiveness throughout its service life, but the Stooping Hawk's ongoing battlefield success ensured its survival in the touman.

The Wars of Reaving brought catastrophe to Clan Blood Spirit, culminating in the Clan's Annihilation. However, the Stooping Hawk itself survived the destruction of its parent Clan. Clan Stone Lion, newly formed from the remnants of the Reaving-era upheaval and operating from a similar position of resource scarcity, sought out and captured the York OmniMech Y1 Facility to secure production of the Stooping Hawk. For the Stone Lions, the design's reputation as a low-cost, sturdy OmniMech made it an ideal cornerstone for rebuilding their touman in the post-Reaving Homeworld Clans.

text.deployment: Alternate Configuration A transforms the Strider into a dedicated targeting and spotting platform for missile-heavy formations. Twin Narc missile beacon launchers allow the 'Mech to designate targets for allied indirect fire, while a TAG laser designator enables Arrow IV artillery and semi-guided LRM coordination. A Beagle active probe and C3 slave unit complete the electronics suite, sharing targeting data across the network. The single small laser represents the configuration's only true weapon, emphasizing its support role over direct combat capability.

Alternate Configuration B provides straightforward long-range fire support through twin LRM-10 launchers with dedicated ammunition bins. This simple but effective loadout allows the Strider to contribute meaningful firepower to engagements beyond normal medium 'Mech range, softening targets before friendly units close to decisive distance. The configuration lacks sophisticated electronics, relying on the base chassis' standard targeting systems to guide its missile volleys.

Alternate Configuration C combines indirect fire capability with direct energy weapons for a versatile long-range loadout. Twin LRM-5 launchers provide harassment fire while a large laser delivers precise damage at extended ranges. A C3 slave unit integrates the Strider into combined-arms networks, allowing allied units to benefit from its forward position. This configuration balances ammunition dependency with energy weapon reliability.

Alternate Configuration D optimizes the Strider for close-range combat supported by comprehensive electronic warfare systems. Twin Streak SRM-2 launchers ensure ammunition efficiency while two medium pulse lasers provide accurate backup firepower. The configuration includes a Beagle active probe, TAG designator, and C3 slave unit, making it effective as both a direct combatant and a network node. A single small laser rounds out the weapons loadout.

Alternate Configuration E maximizes short-range striking power through twin Streak SRM-6 launchers backed by a single medium laser. The Streak systems ensure no missile is wasted on missed shots, making this configuration particularly ammunition-efficient despite its heavy missile loadout. The advent of larger Streak launcher systems reinforced the Strider's image as a light missile support unit while significantly increasing its effectiveness in combat.

Alternate Configuration F, nicknamed the "Grand Jenner" by DCMS warriors, is widely considered the most effective standard Strider loadout. Twin Streak SRM-4 launchers combine with two medium lasers to provide balanced firepower, while six jump jets grant 180 meters of jumping capability. This combination of missiles, lasers, and mobility creates a configuration strikingly similar to the famous Jenner light 'Mech, hence the affectionate nickname. Many pilots consider the F configuration to offer the best balance of the Strider's capabilities.

Alternate Configuration G emerged during the Jihad, mounting twin MML-7 launchers capable of firing either long-range or short-range missile volleys depending on tactical needs. Twin ER small lasers provide anti-infantry capability while CASE protection guards against ammunition explosions. This flexible loadout allows pilots to adapt their engagement profile based on mission requirements without reconfiguring the entire 'Mech.

Alternate Configuration H is a Dark Age era advancement, mounting twin Clan-specification Streak LRM-10 launchers. These advanced missile systems combine the range of standard LRMs with Streak technology's guaranteed accuracy, dramatically improving the Strider's long-range effectiveness. The configuration demonstrates the increasing availability of Clan technology to Inner Sphere manufacturers in the post-Jihad era.

Alternate Configuration M serves as a dedicated command and control platform, carrying twin C3 boosted master computers. This configuration transforms the Strider into a mobile network hub capable of coordinating multiple C3-equipped lances simultaneously. While lightly armed for direct combat, the M configuration's value lies in the tactical advantages it provides to allied forces through enhanced targeting data sharing.

Alternate Configuration R emerged as a field upgrade during Operation Bulldog, utilizing captured Clan Smoke Jaguar weapons to bolster SLDF forces in later campaign waves. Based on the E configuration's layout, the R mounts twin Clan-specification Streak SRM-6 launchers paired with two Clan medium pulse lasers. The lighter weight of Clan weaponry allows this configuration to deliver firepower exceeding any standard Inner Sphere loadout.

Alternate Configuration X mounts an experimental Bombast laser alongside twin MML-3 launchers with both LRM and SRM ammunition. The Bombast laser's variable damage output provides flexibility in engaging different target types, while the smaller MML systems offer supplementary firepower without excessive weight. CASE protection guards the ammunition bays, and the configuration serves primarily as a testbed for emerging weapons technologies.

text.overview:
The Striker is an eighty-ton assault BattleMech introduced in 2571 by Stormvanger Assemblies Unlimited for the Star League Defense Force. One of the first assault designs built specifically for the non-Royal SLDF House formations, the Striker filled a critical political and military need, allowing House Lords to reserve their own assault 'Mechs while still equipping SLDF units with capable heavy firepower. The design quickly became one of the most common assault 'Mechs in SLDF service, with many historians crediting its production for helping cement the early Star League.

Despite its rugged construction and solid combat record, the Striker was marginal compared to later assault designs and was gradually relegated to militia and second-line duty. With production long since ended and fewer than three hundred known to survive by the late thirty-first century, the Striker endures as a reflection of Star League-era engineering and the value of simple, maintainable design.
text.capabilities:
The Striker compared very favorably to its assault-class contemporaries such as the Victor and Emperor, offering maneuverability comparable to many medium 'Mechs thanks to its Pitban 320 fusion engine. This mobility advantage came at no sacrifice to firepower, as the design carries an impressive array of weapons effective across multiple engagement ranges. At long range, the HellStar PPC and Pontiac Light Class 5 Autocannon provide sustained fire capable of softening targets well before they can close. The Defiance B3L Large Laser adds significant punch at medium range, while three Hellion-b II Medium Lasers give the Striker respectable close-range defenses.

This versatility is both the Striker's greatest strength and its most notable limitation. Firing all weapons simultaneously generates heat that exceeds the capacity of its fifteen standard heat sinks, forcing MechWarriors to carefully manage their rate of fire during sustained engagements. The thirteen and a half tons of Leviathan Plus armor provide solid protection for an assault 'Mech, though not exceptional by the standards of heavier designs.

The Striker's true value lies in its rugged construction and use of common, easily-sourced components. This Easy to Maintain design philosophy kept these 'Mechs operational across centuries of declining industrial capacity, long after the factory that produced them had been destroyed.
text.deployment: Introduced by the Capellan Confederation during the Dark Age, this extensive refit replaces the original weapons array entirely in favor of plasma rifles, paired with heat-dissipating armor that helps manage the substantial thermal output of the plasma weaponry. This configuration transforms the venerable Striker into a dedicated heat-warfare platform, capable of dealing significant damage while simultaneously overheating enemy 'Mechs and vehicles. The STC-2L represents the Confederation's continued commitment to extracting maximum combat value from the ancient Striker chassis through the application of advanced technology.
text.battleHistory:
The Striker's origins trace back to a deliberate political calculation by First Lord Ian Cameron. While all the Great Houses fielded assault BattleMechs by the time of the Striker's introduction in 2571, these machines were relatively scarce and reserved for the most prestigious units or highest-ranking officers. Terran Hegemony units, equipped with far more powerful designs, created a disparity in firepower between Royal and House SLDF formations that bred resentment. Cameron ordered full-scale production of the Striker to address this imbalance, and the 'Mech quickly filled the ranks of the SLDF's House-donated regiments.

The strategy succeeded. The addition of capable assault 'Mechs to donated formations generated goodwill among the Great Houses, and many historians credit the Striker's proliferation with convincing reluctant House Lords to commit additional units to the SLDF. However, as technological advances allowed the Star League to field larger and more capable assault designs, the Striker was steadily displaced from frontline service. The Awesome, produced by Technicron Manufacturing beginning in 2665 as a direct replacement, rendered the Striker obsolete for first-line duty. Most surviving Strikers were deployed among militia units in the Rimward section of the Hegemony.

The fall of the Star League and the onset of the Succession Wars scattered surviving Strikers across the Inner Sphere. The destruction of Stormvanger's Caph facility in 2867 ended any hope of renewed production, and the remaining machines became increasingly rare prizes. By the late thirty-first century, fewer than three hundred Strikers remained operational, concentrated primarily among Steiner and Liao formations.

Capellan units deployed their Strikers in frontline roles, with many receiving field upgrades that kept them competitive against more modern designs. The Capellan Confederation Armed Forces proved particularly adept at extracting continued value from the aging chassis, developing dedicated refit programs through Earthwerks Ltd. on Grand Base. Steiner forces typically relegated their Strikers to militia and garrison duty, where the design's low maintenance requirements proved well-suited to under-resourced commands. The Word of Blake also fielded Strikers among their formations during the Jihad, where the ancient design continued to perform respectably against more modern opponents. Into the Dark Age, the Capellans continued to invest in the Striker platform, introducing new variants that leveraged advanced technology to keep the five-century-old chassis relevant on the modern battlefield.

production.manufacturer: Eagle Craft Group, St. Louis MechWorks, Svarstaad Industriplex Gamma

text.notes: Features the following Quirks: Improved Communications, Ubiquitous

Dev Note: The various TRO and RS entries from Golden Century don't match in terms of heat sink placement, pod space, etc. I went with the fix that requires no changes to the Record sheets provided, which gives it 11 fixed heat sinks and 24 pod space, rather than a fixed DHS in the LL that doesn't show up on 2 out of 3 configs.

text.deployment: Alternate Configuration A is built for long-range fire support, pairing a Gauss rifle with an ER PPC for powerful direct-fire engagements at extended range. Three LRM-5 launchers provide supplementary indirect fire capability in support of allied units. Two medium pulse lasers offer adequate close-range self-defense against lighter opponents. The Alpha and Prime configurations often deploy together in pairs, with the Alpha providing sustained long-range support while the Prime closes for decisive short-range engagements.

Alternate Configuration B is purpose-built as a command and control platform, mounting two C3 master computers that enable coordination of up to three full lances of networked 'Mechs. This configuration is intended to deploy and safeguard the central C3 node of an entire company-level formation. An LRM-20 and an LRM-10 provide long-range bombardment capability, while two medium pulse lasers and two medium lasers offer short-range defensive firepower. The heavy reliance on long-range missiles makes this configuration vulnerable to aggressive rushing attacks.

Alternate Configuration C takes advantage of advanced DCMS missile systems to deliver withering firepower at close and medium ranges. An MRM-40 and MRM-30 can overwhelm enemy defenses with sheer volume of fire, while a pair of Streak SRM-4 launchers and a medium laser provide supplementary close-range punch. A C3 slave unit enables this configuration to function as part of a networked lance for maximum efficiency. The primary drawback is a heavy dependence on ammunition that can force withdrawal before an engagement concludes.

Alternate Configuration D was first deployed in Kuritan and Davion cities, mounting an LB 20-X autocannon supported by two PPCs for effective engagement across multiple range brackets. Uniquely among Sunder configurations, the D variant carries three jump jets, granting mobility uncommon for an assault 'Mech and allowing it to traverse difficult urban terrain. This combination proved extremely deadly when the LB 20-X's cluster rounds could be combined with torso-mounted jump jet mobility to achieve unexpected firing angles.

Alternate Configuration E mounts paired Snub-Nose PPCs and Streak SRM-6 launchers, backed by an ER medium laser and an LB 10-X autocannon. This loadout provides a balanced mix of direct-fire energy weapons and ballistic punch effective from short to medium range. The configuration may represent a factory-built refinement of the mixed-technology R variant developed during Operation Bulldog, achieving a similar combat profile using exclusively Inner Sphere production components.

Introduced during the Dark Age era, Alternate Configuration F incorporates a C3 boosted slave unit for enhanced network coordination. The offensive loadout combines five Clan-built LRM-5 launchers with six Thunderbolt-5 missile launchers, creating a sustained barrage of precision and saturation fire at long range. A single Clan-manufactured ER medium laser provides close-range backup. This configuration reflects the increasing availability of Clan-spec components to Inner Sphere manufacturers during the post-Jihad reconstruction period.

Another Dark Age era addition, Alternate Configuration G stands as a significant escalation in the Sunder's combat capability. A Clan-built ER PPC and Clan LB 20-X autocannon provide tremendous direct-fire punch, supplemented by a Clan ER medium laser. The configuration's most notable feature is a TSEMP cannon, capable of disabling enemy electronics and systems with electromagnetic pulses. A C3 boosted slave unit allows the G variant to share its advanced targeting data across the lance network, making it both a powerful individual combatant and a force multiplier for allied units.

The R configuration is a mixed-technology field upgrade developed in the midst of Operation Bulldog, utilizing captured Clan Smoke Jaguar weapons to bolster SLDF forces during later campaign waves. Twin Clan large pulse lasers provide devastating medium-range firepower, supported by an LB 10-X autocannon. Four ER medium lasers and a pair of Streak SRM-6 launchers round out a weapons array that finally allowed the Sunder to match Clan assault OmniMechs in raw combat effectiveness, a milestone for Inner Sphere OmniMech development.

The X configuration employs experimental technology, mounting eight Enhanced LRM-5 launchers fed by a C3 slave unit for improved targeting data. B-Pods in each leg provide point defense against battle armor swarms, while three ER medium lasers and a medium pulse laser offer direct-fire capability for targets within the Enhanced LRM minimum range envelope. This experimental loadout trades proven reliability for increased long-range saturation capability, typical of DCMS weapons testing programs.

text.overview: Star Colonel Rikkard Nova Cat pounced on OvKhan Kalasa’s offer to build the iconic Nova Cat Supernova on Angell II. Combining its classic lasers with the endo-steel chassis and heavy armor of late model Supernovas, Delta Aimag still found the space to carry four Coolant Pods by slightly reducing the number of heat sinks. The shocking result was a Supernova that could fire all its weapons without overheating. Unfortunately for Rikkard, Delta Aimag has claimed most of the Supernovas as payment for the factory. Rikkard’s loss is the Inner Sphere’s gain as Clan Sea Fox sells the Supernova far and wide.
text.notableUnits: Captain Bryant Flynn Dunham: The Fourth Regulan Hussars hit Marik in July 3147. Captain “BFD” was happy to see that the defending Clan Protectorate’s Purifier Cluster faced him in direct combat. Implementing his infamous motto of “hey diddle diddle, right up the middle,” his Marauder came face to face with a Protectorate Supernova. Thankfully, the Supernova overheated in the process of dismantling BFD’s ride and was swarmed by Leonidas battle armor. Dunham claimed the fallen ’Mech and pushed on with his unit. At the Winter Palace in Dormuth the Fourth ran into the Shiva Keshik, which scythed through them until BFD made a stand. Utilizing the Supernova’s coolant pods better than its previous pilot, he held the center of the field, acting as a rallying point until the Thirtieth Hussars could come to their aid. Ultimately pushed back after Colonel Mejia’s dishonorable actions, BFD was able to retreat in good order and kept his Supernova when the Hussars were granted hegira in August.

text.overview:
The Talon was first deployed in 2670 to provide light BattleMech companies with much-needed long-range firepower. Star League High Command was so impressed by the design during combat trials in 2669 that they immediately ordered full production, and sales to the SLDF quickly surpassed all other light BattleMechs. Commonly paired with the lighter Mongoose, the Talon provided covering fire should the reconnaissance unit encounter something it could not handle on its own.

Rendered extinct during the Succession Wars, the Talon was absent from the battlefield for over two centuries before Blackstone BattleMechs restarted production on Inarcs in 3056. The once-popular design quickly reestablished itself as a valued asset in light formations, earning renewed respect for its combination of speed and long-range hitting power.
text.capabilities:
The Talon combines impressive speed with heavy long-range firepower, a rare combination in the light weight class. An Edasich Motors 280-rated extra-light engine propels the thirty-five ton machine to a maximum speed of nearly 130 kilometers per hour, allowing it to keep pace with virtually any reconnaissance unit. Blackstone markets the design as being able to outrun anything it cannot outgun.

The primary weapon is a Lord's Light-2 extended-range PPC, giving the Talon an engagement range approaching 700 meters. For close-range defense, a pair of ChisComp 39 medium lasers mounted on the left arm provide adequate firepower against other light 'Mechs. Seven and a half tons of Kallon Light Shield A standard armor give the Talon excellent protection for its weight class, enough durability to weather return fire while withdrawing from unfavorable engagements.

The design sacrifices jump capability entirely, relying on raw speed for maneuverability. The absence of jump jets can leave the Talon vulnerable in rough terrain, but on open ground its combination of speed, reach, and staying power make it a formidable opponent for anything in its weight class.
text.deployment: This apocryphal variant is a heavily downgraded Succession Wars-era Talon, reportedly fielded by militia forces during the Clan Invasion of 3050. With the original extra-light engine replaced by a standard GM 210, this variant sacrifices considerable speed, reaching a maximum of only 90 kilometers per hour. The design retains a standard PPC for ranged combat and a pair of medium lasers for close defense, with seven and a half tons of standard armor. Without lower arm actuators, the 'Mech can flip its arm weapons into the rear arc. The variant highlights the desperate measures taken by militia forces to keep aging Star League designs operational long after spare parts became unavailable.
text.battleHistory:
The Talon first saw action shortly after its introduction in 2670 and quickly proved itself invaluable to light 'Mech companies across the Star League Defense Force. Its long-range firepower filled a critical gap that had long plagued light formations, which traditionally relied on speed and numbers rather than hitting power. By the late Star League era, the Talon was among the most ordered light BattleMechs in SLDF service.

The TLN-5W upgrade in 2760 initially saw distribution restricted to Royal units. The Amaris Civil War changed this, with the TLN-5V distributed widely among regular SLDF formations and the upgraded TLN-5W seeing frontline service for the first time. Following the Exodus, every Successor State sought to acquire Talons as fast as they could be manufactured. Commanders attempted to replicate the original SLDF lance tactic of deploying three Talons alongside a Mongoose for headhunting and supply disruption behind enemy lines, substituting a Spector to flush out enemy commanders when Mongooses were unavailable.

The harshness of the Succession Wars proved too great for the design's survival. Production at the Briden BattleMechs Unlimited facility on Errai never kept pace with losses during the First Succession War. When several tactical nuclear strikes destroyed the factory in 2815, the Talon's fate was sealed. The last operational example was stripped for parts around 2830 to keep a House Kurita light lance functional.

The Inner Sphere would not see another Talon for over two centuries. In 3056, Blackstone BattleMechs announced they had secured production rights and restarted manufacturing at their facility on Inarcs. Sent to the Clan occupation zone border, the reborn Talon first saw combat during the Jade Falcon invasion of Coventry, where reports of its performance were highly favorable. During the FedCom Civil War, elements of the Seventh Crucis Lancers damaged Blackstone's production lines on Inarcs in 3065, though they returned to full capacity by late 3066.

Following the Civil War, the Lyran Alliance opened the Talon for export, recognizing that most Lyran units preferred traditional heavier formations. The Federated Suns and mercenary units absorbed much of the demand, while ComStar, the Free Rasalhague Republic, and the Draconis Combine acquired lances for evaluation. A few of these combined-arms lances have been spotted along the Jade Falcon border, though no command has fielded Talons in the numbers the original SLDF once did. Blackstone continued developing new variants through the Jihad and into the Dark Age, keeping the venerable design relevant with successive technological improvements.

text.deployment: Produced under the auspices of the Clan Protectorate, the Tempest C melds the proven Inner Sphere chassis and armor with a mix of Inner Sphere and Clan-specification weaponry. A Clan-grade large pulse laser and Gauss rifle replace their Inner Sphere counterparts in the arm mounts, while three standard medium lasers are retained. An ATM-9 launcher mounted in the left torso provides tactical flexibility through its variable ammunition types, though only two tons of ammunition somewhat limit this advantage. As with all previous Tempest designs, no CASE has been fitted, a persistent vulnerability that Clan warriors have noted with some disapproval.

production.manufacturer: Irian BattleMechs Unlimited, Irian BattleMechs Unlimited

text.deployment: Regarded as a difficult design to improve upon, it took until the 3130s for Irian BattleMechs Unlimited to produce a formal successor variant. The TMP-4M retains the standard medium lasers and Gauss rifle of the original TMP-3M but replaces the SRM-6 and large pulse laser with five improved jump jets and a snub-nosed PPC. This configuration transforms the Tempest into a more capable skirmisher, with the improved jump jets providing superior mobility while the snub-nosed PPC offers a devastating close-range energy complement to the Gauss rifle's long-range kinetic firepower.

This custom configuration features a complete suite of Clan-specification weaponry, mounting a Clan ER PPC and Clan ER medium laser in each arm, with a Clan ER Small Laser and Clan Streak SRM-6 in the torso. A targeting computer enhances the accuracy of the energy weapons, while four additional double heat sinks manage the thermal output of the upgraded arsenal. The weight savings from Clan technology allow this configuration to achieve firepower levels that would be impossible with Inner Sphere equivalents within the Templar III's twenty-nine ton pod capacity.

Alternate Configuration A is configured for intermediate to short-range combat, mounting a pair of large pulse lasers and two medium pulse lasers as its primary energy weapons. A pair of seven-tube Multi-Missile Launchers with two tons of ammunition provides flexible fire support across multiple range brackets, allowing the pilot to select optimal ammunition types for the engagement.
